hints: Placing the largest remaining value first creates one inversion with each smaller remaining value.
Use as many of those inversions as possible while k is large.
When fewer than the maximum remain, place one appropriately ranked value and then list the rest increasingly.
analogy: Each selected value spends one inversion for every smaller unused value left behind it.
example: For n=4 and k=4, output [4,2,1,3]: 4 contributes 3 inversions and 2 contributes 1.
algorithm: Maintain the unused numbers as an ordered sequence. At each position with r numbers remaining, choose the (min(k,r-1)+1)-th smallest unused number, subtract that many smaller unused numbers from k, and remove it. A Fenwick tree supports selection, or exploit the greedy structure to output full descending largest values followed by one pivot and the remaining values increasingly.
correctness: The chosen value creates exactly one inversion with each smaller unused number. The greedy spends at most r-1 inversions per position and always leaves a feasible remainder; after all positions the total spent is the original k.
complexity: For n values, O(n) time and O(1) extra space with the descending-prefix construction, excluding output.
